correctness.rationale: Every Ω(n)≤2 integer n≥2 is prime p, p², or pq with distinct p<q. Factorial divisibility gives S(p)=p, S(p²)=2p (including p=2), and S(pq)=q. For p≥5, p!>p²; for prime squares (2p)!>p⁴ including n=4; for distinct pq, the cases q=3,5 yield exceptions 6,15 only, while for q≥7 the ratio F(q)=q!/(q²(q−2)²) exceeds F(7)>1 and increases, hence q!>p²q². Together 2,3 are the prime exceptions. Independent exact least-factorial valuation and comparison checked 17,243 Ω≤2 values through 50,000 with precisely [2,3,6,15]; no infinite conclusion inferred from cutoff.
